name: Did It Work?

brand.tagline: Every big policy promised something. See what it promised, what the evaluations found since, and how the verdict moved. Run on Ultrastable, the foundation for any autonomous system.

idea: A casebook of policies and programmes worldwide, each with its stated aim in its own words, the evaluations published since, graded by design, and a running verdict. A daily beat searches open evaluation and trial registries for each case, adds new evaluations, re-grades the verdict when evidence piles up, and logs every change of verdict with its reason.
goals: casebook of 40 policies with stated aims and graded evaluations
verdict history and follow on any case
prediction market of the system's own: forecast the next evaluation, scored when it lands
positioning: Policies are judged by their announcements, not their results; holding each one to its own stated aim, as evaluations arrive, changes how people argue about the next one. Same shape as Unlearn and Practical Solutions: guess first, graded evidence, a loop that keeps checking, no accounts or trackers.

system_test.loop: A daily beat searches open evaluation and trial registries for each case, adds new evaluations, re-grades the verdict when evidence piles up, and logs every change of verdict with its reason.
system_test.measure: share of cases whose evaluations were searched within 7 days, target 1.0; verdict changes logged with a reason, never silent
system_test.upkeep: new studies, data releases and evaluations arrive every week, sources rot and entries must be re-graded
system_test.run_cost: 5 USD a month for the back end

depth.public_good: Citizens, journalists and staff can hold policy to its own promises, so public money moves to what works; it empowers voters with evidence.
